title: Refactor rollback checklist + mini hypotheses
content:
Purpose:
This is my quick scratchpad for rolling back a recent refactor (PR #2147) if it shows regressions in production. Not a formal runbook — more of a checklist + short hypotheses to test while we triage.

Context:
- Refactor touched batching logic (batching manager) and KV-cache warmup path.
- Deployed to canary (10% traffic) 2024-10-18; alerted on elevated p99 and occasional OOMs on n1-small-gpu pools.
- Canary logs show increased KV-cache miss ratio and longer time-to-first-token for some clients.

Quick decision matrix (fast):
- If p99 latency >= baseline * 1.3 OR error_rate >= 0.5% absolute increase -> rollback to previous deployment.
- If OOMs detected on >= 2 nodes in same AZ within 10m -> rollback.
- If correctness regressions (wrong output format / missing keys in function-calls) observed in > 0.1% requests -> immediate rollback.

Rollback checklist (order of operations):
- [ ] Confirm metrics (source: Redwood Console - route-level dashboard): p50/p95/p99, error rate, request rate, mem usage, batch size distribution, kv-cache hit%.
- [ ] Snapshot current canary deployment ID + commit SHA. (kubectl get deploy -n runtime canary -o yaml -> save commit label)
- [ ] Notify: post to #runtime-incident with short TL;DR + command to watch logs. Tag on-call (Aisha).
- [ ] If decision = rollback, trigger: GH Actions workflow "deploy-rollout/rollback" with target sha = previous-stable.
- [ ] Post-rollback smoke test script: run smoke.sh against canary endpoint (included below). Validate: 10 warmup requests, 100 parallel small requests, one long-sequence request.
- [ ] Monitor for 30 minutes post-rollback: metrics should converge; collect 30m logs bundle for postmortem.
- [ ] Create postmortem stub in Confluence + JIRA issue if rollback occurred (link in linked_artifacts).
- [ ] Assign follow-ups: unit tests for batching edgecases, add observability for kv-cache warmup timings, add synthetic canary checks for time-to-first-token.

Quick commands (cheat sheet):
- Check deploy label: kubectl -n runtime get deploy canary -o jsonpath='{.metadata.labels.commit}'
- Trigger rollback (manual GH action): https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/actions/workflows/deploy-rollout.yml
- Tail logs for err/oome: kubectl -n runtime logs -l app=serving-canary -f --tail=200 | grep -E "OOM|Exception|KVCache"

Smoke test (local):
- ./scripts/smoke.sh --endpoint https://canary.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate --token $TEST_TOKEN
- smoke.sh: warmup 10x small, parallel 100x small, single 1x 2048-token generation -> measure ttf (time-to-first-token).

Mini hypotheses to run through while triaging (these are quick, not exhaustive):
1) Hypothesis: batching manager change increased variance in batch sizes -> more long tails -> p99 up.
   Quick checks: batch size histogram in console vs baseline; compare median batch size and spikes.
   Quick mitigation without rollback: reduce max_batch_window_ms to prior value via feature flag.

2) Hypothesis: KV-cache warmup now does lazy initialization which causes first requests to miss and block longer (time-to-first-token increase).
   Quick checks: kv-cache hit% over time, logs for "kv-init" events.
   Mitigation: flip feature flag to eager-warm or revert kv warmup commit.

3) Hypothesis: subtle serialization change in request envelope caused extra CPU work on model workers (higher CPU -> slower response).
   Quick checks: compare request size distribution, CPU per-pod before/after.
   Mitigation: revert serialization patch or reintroduce previous marshalling path.

4) Hypothesis: memory leak in new batching data structure -> OOMs under load.
   Quick checks: heap/profile snapshot, increase in RSS over time during replay.
   Mitigation: rollback required if OOM rate high; otherwise roll-forward with memory fixes only after reproducing locally.

Observability additions to consider (quick backlog items):
- Add metric: "batching.queue_wait_ms" percentile per route.
- Track: kv-cache initialization latency and who triggered.
- Synthetic canary test that asserts ttf < X ms for warm and cold paths.
- Alert: kv-cache-miss-rate > 5% for 5m -> page.

Post-rollback notes (what I will collect):
- Logs from canary at commit SHA (pre-rollback) + post-rollback commit. Zip and attach to JIRA.
- Heap/profile from affected pod(s) if available (pprof snapshots).
- Repro script and load pattern that caused OOMs / tail latency.

Follow-ups (TODO list):
- [ ] Add unit tests for edge batching sizes (0, 1, 2, large) and ensure path parity. (owner: Diego)
- [ ] Add integration test for kv-cache warmup (small harness) and mock remote model to measure ttf. (owner: Gregory)
- [ ] Add console chart: batch size distribution per route; set alert thresholds. (owner: Observability)
- [ ] Document feature flag gating and rollback playbook in Confluence. (owner: eng-docs)

Notes-to-self: keep this lightweight. If rollback occurs, prioritize restore of customer SLA over deep investigations. We can run deeper repros after stability restored.

Random scribbles / quick experiments to try while triaging:
- Replay canary traffic locally with --kv-cold to simulate cold misses. Script: tools/replay.py --trace canary-trace.json --concurrency 50
- Instrument batcher to log batch sizes at DEBUG for 10m window to capture distribution.
- Try toggling FEATURE_EAGER_KV_WARMUP=false via env in canary pods and rolling restart subset (kubectl set env deploy/canary FEATURE_EAGER_KV_WARMUP=false) then observe.

End of scratchpad. Keep short, update as we learn more.

-- greg
